title: When You Don’t See Your Value — Psalm 139:14
paragraphs: When You Don’t See Your Value — Psalm 139:14
You look in the mirror and see “not enough.”

God looks at you and says, “fearfully and wonderfully made.”
That is not poetry to decorate a wall.
That is truth to pull a soul out of the dark.

Psalm 139:14 is for the person who feels invisible.
For the one who keeps shrinking in rooms God never asked them to shrink in.
For the one smiling outside but bleeding inside.
For the one who learned to measure worth by attention, applause, body shape, achievements, or how badly someone failed to love them.

Your value was never supposed to be decided by broken people.
Not by rejection.
Not by comparison.
Not by your worst mistake.
Not by the silence of those who should have affirmed you.
Your worth was spoken by God before insecurity ever learned your name.

David said, “I praise You because I am fearfully and wonderfully made; Your works are wonderful, I know that full well.”
He did not say, “I praise You because I feel confident today.”
He rooted his identity in God’s workmanship, not his emotions.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because sometimes the real reason we do not see our value is not just pain.
It is shame.
We have believed that our sin, our past, our failures, or our scars erased the image of God in us.

Jesus stepped into our ruin, carried our sin to the cross, and proved that souls this broken are still worth dying for.
The cross settles the question of your value.
If Christ shed His blood to redeem you, then you are not trash, not forgotten, not disposable.

Yes, sin must be repented of.
Yes, identity must be surrendered to Christ.
But in Him, you are not what wounded you.
You are not what trapped you.
You are not what they called you.

In Christ, you are known.
In Christ, you are wanted.
In Christ, you are being remade.

So breathe.
Stand up.
And stop speaking about yourself like God made a mistake.

You are His creation.
And in Jesus, you can become His redeemed masterpiece.

Prayer:
Lord, when I cannot see my worth, remind me that You are my Maker and my Redeemer. Break every lie that tells me I am worthless. Teach me to see myself through the truth of Your Word and the mercy of the cross. In Jesus’ name, amen.
